questions.question_text: An epidemic of wide geographical distribution is known as
questions.explanation:
The usual prevalence of a disease in a community is called the baseline prevalence. If the baseline is a low to moderate level and continues
without signi�cant �uctuation, the disease is said to be endemic in the community. A persistent but high level of baseline is called hyper
endemic occurrence. Most psychiatric disorders are low level endemic disorders (with exceptions). An irregular pattern of signi�cant
�uctuation from baseline is called sporadic occurrence. When the occurrence within an area clearly exceeds the expected level in a given
time period, it is called an epidemic. An epidemic can be slow and steady rising epidemic as in the case of multifactorial chronic diseases or
acute outbreaks as in infectious diseases. A pandemic is an epidemic in wide geographical proportion g. HIV pandemic.

questions.question_text: Most common level of prevention currently employed in psychiatric practice is
questions.explanation:
In current psychiatric practice, our knowledge of risk factors and causal insults is limited. Hence most prevention in psychiatric practice is of
tertiary nature Early intervention program in psychosis is an example of secondary prevention. Public health initiatives such as eradication
of poverty, maintaining healthy diet etc could prevent certain, at least milder forms of mental illnesses - these could be termed as primary
prevention strategies. Interventions aimed at high risk groups are usually secondary preventions. Rehabilitation is a tertiary prevention
(reducing disabilities).

questions.question_text:
The incidence of schizophrenia is three times higher in migrants, but this drops to 1.8 times higher than natives when point prevalence rates
are considered. This can be explained by

options.text: Better access to care for natives
Shorter duration of illness in migrants

correct_answer.text: Shorter duration of illness in migrants

questions.explanation:
For illnesses which are signi�cantly chronic (e.g. schizophrenia), prevalence will be higher compared to those illnesses which are acute and
short-lived (g. in�uenza), even if the incidence rates are comparable. Hence a simple expression Prevalence = incidence X duration of illness
explains the relationship between incidence and prevalence. One explanation for disparity observed in migrants to natives ratio of incidence
and prevalence may relate to the relatively shorter duration of psychoses in immigrants. This is hypothetical and not a widely established
explanation.

questions.question_text:
The annual incidence of injected cocaine use is estimated to be 20/100,000. The annual mortality rate is 4/100,000; if point prevalence is
80/100,000 what is the calculated duration of cocaine use?
questions.explanation:
Prevalence = incidence X duration of illness explains the relationship between incidence and prevalence. If we discard the very small
mortality rate of 4/100,000, and apply the above formula, 80=20 X (?), we can arrive at Duration = 4 years.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is expressed as number of new cases per person-year of observation?
questions.explanation:
Incidence (of a disease in year 2008 at an area A) = Number of newly diagnosed cases in year 2008 / Mid 2008 population at area A.
Incidence is a ratio measured against time. One month incidence will be invariably lower than one year incidence. The most common
measurement of incidence using the above formula is also known as cumulative incidence. This is valid in cohort studies where attrition is
low, but not so useful when attrition is signi�cant. This is because dropouts are excluded from being counted as new cases, while the
denominator population usually takes them into account. To avoid this problem, incidence density (also known as incidence rate) is used. It
expresses number of new cases per person-year of observation. The unit of the incidence rate is rather bizarre, given by person-time units.
Hence incidence rates are often used in reporting results that compare two groups incidence rates - providing a ratio with no units.

questions.question_text: There are 65 suicides in a population of 1300 patients with schizophrenia. The rate 65/1300 refers to which one of the following?
questions.explanation:
Cause-speci�c mortality rate: g. alcohol speci�c mortality. This refers to ratio between number of deaths due to alcohol in a population and
total population size. Case-fatality rate: Ratio between number of deaths due to a speci�c disease and number of persons a�ected by the
disease in a population. It is a measure of the fatal severity of the disease studies. For example, 15 patients out of 100 with anorexia will die
due to its complications. Proportionate mortality rate: It is a measure of contribution of a disease to societal mortality burden. It is given by
the ratio between deaths due to a speci�c cause and total number of deaths in a population. In this question, out of 1300 persons in a
population with schizophrenia, death due to suicide (cause) is 65. Hence 65/1300 is cause speci�c mortality rate. [Note that these 65 did not
die because of schizophrenia - the cause of their death is suicide]. In a similar fashion one can expand this to stroke-speci�c mortality in
schizophrenia, Myocardial infarction speci�c rate etc.

Lifetime prevalence is "the proportion of individuals in the population who have ever manifested a disorder, who are alive on a given day.

disorder during entire period (often a speci�ed period, de�ned by the life expectancy of the population studied) of their lif LMR includes the

questions.question_text: The phenomenon of relative deprivation is explained by
questions.explanation:
A scoring system developed by the British general practitioner Brian Jarman for the level of social deprivation in a community, using census
data on percentages of old people living alone, single-parent families, children younger than 5 years of age, unskilled and unemployed
persons, ethnic minorities, overcrowded dwellings, changes of address in previous year, etc. Although a valid indicator, it is not generally
accepted outside the United Kingdom.

questions.question_text:
In 1999, 50 cases of CJD had been linked to French-derived hGH, from a cohort of 1500 patients. Of these 12 died at the time of the survey.
Calculate the attack rate for CJD transmission in this cohort.
questions.explanation:
Attack rate is given by number of cases that develop divided by number exposed in a cohort (at risk). It is simply an incidence rate following
an acute exposure.
